baseline.entry_point: nq_open -> DPR query -> Wiki-DPR Top-50 -> frozen QORE Top-5
baseline.equivalence_test: selection and retrieval settings are identical to the frozen Phase 9B path; only global passage IDs and source evidence labels are observed

core_invariants: The audit is observation-only and never feeds gold labels or alignment statistics into retrieval, selection, generation, or evaluator code.
The nq_open validation[200:250] slice, compressed Wiki-DPR corpus, nprobe=64, DPR Answer Scorer, QORE K=5, and seed=42 are frozen.
Strict gold evidence requires original NQ document title plus short-answer token span text; support evidence is reported separately and cannot upgrade strict evidence.
The full-corpus scan retains only canonical passage IDs in the private alignment cache; compact exchange output contains no question, passage, answer, or prediction text.

interfaces.output_schema: document title, strict short-span answer tokens, support answer fallback, mapping source
invariants: Question text is used only for local join and is never emitted.

interfaces.output_schema: question ID -> strict/support global passage ID sets
invariants: Title equality and token-boundary answer matching are deterministic.

interfaces.input_schema: frozen Top-50 retrieval and QORE Top-5 local rows plus global alignment index
interfaces.output_schema: gold counts, Top-50/Top-5 coverage, retrieval hit, selected hit, conditional selection recall
invariants: Selection receives only the original DPR/Answer Scorer inputs and never the gold alignment.

plugins.insertion_point: before the diagnostic join, outside production RAG
plugins.hypothesis: Original NQ title and short-answer spans provide a stricter evidence label than answer-string occurrence alone.

plugins.insertion_point: full Wiki-DPR metadata scan, independent of selector
plugins.hypothesis: A question's gold passage coverage can be measured by global Wiki-DPR IDs rather than answer-string heuristics.
plugins.input_schema: Wiki-DPR id/title/text rows and GoldEvidence map
plugins.output_schema: strict/support passage ID sets and title-seen counts
plugins.resource_estimate: one full Wiki-DPR metadata scan; no generator calls

plugins.insertion_point: after unchanged retrieval and unchanged QORE selection
plugins.hypothesis: Separating Top-50 coverage from QORE Top-5 coverage identifies whether the next intervention belongs to retrieval or selection.
plugins.input_schema: retrieved global IDs, selected global IDs, aligned strict/support IDs
plugins.resource_estimate: 50 questions, 50 retrieval rows and 5 selected rows each

composition.merge_rule: Join only by stable nq_i question IDs and canonical global passage IDs; no diagnostic output reaches select_passages.
interaction_ablations: Top-50 retrieval coverage versus QORE Top-5 coverage
answer-string hit heuristic versus title-and-span strict label

validation.baseline_equivalence: Synthetic rows preserve Top-50 and Top-5 IDs while alignment labels are changed only in the observer output.
tests: NQ nested annotation extraction and token-span filtering

reproducibility.dataset_identity: nq_open validation questions 200-249; original NQ validation annotations; Wiki-DPR psgs_w100.nq.compressed
reproducibility.environment: runner records Python executable/version, git revision, config SHA-256, annotation source, corpus config, and cache key

limitations: The strict mapping is title plus exact short-answer span text; it is not a full character-level Wikipedia provenance proof.
Questions with no usable original annotation remain support-only or unmapped and are excluded from strict bottleneck rates.
This audit diagnoses retrieval versus selection coverage; it does not claim a utility improvement or modify production behavior.
